_comment: Pre-registration for scripts/run-import-accuracy.mjs (#980). Committed BEFORE the harness was run on any repository listed under `groups.*.repos.eval`; the prose is benchmarks/IMPORT_RESOLVER_PROTOCOL.md. The harness reads this file, records its sha256 in the report and refuses --save when it differs from the committed copy. A change after the first registered run is a deviation: add it to the Deviation log in the prose with its date and reason. Never edit a value here to make a result look better.

system.under_test: buildFromCwd(tree) from src/graph/builder.js with every family, zero config, on a copy of the pinned commit
system.reference: per group, the language's own tooling (see `groups.*.reference`); never the resolver itself

edge: importing file -> imported file, both repository files, directed; for Swift (module level) importing file -> module:<local SwiftPM target>
universe: the importing files the graph walked AND the reference could analyse; an edge counts only when its importing file is in it

metrics.precision: |graph edges that are also reference edges| / |graph edges|
metrics.recall: |reference edges that are also graph edges| / |reference edges|
metrics.pooling: micro-average over the evaluation repositories of a group

reference.what: the direct includes the compiler reports: clang -E -H -fshow-skipped-includes, the lines of nesting depth one; a header the repository lacks is an error the preprocessor carries on past, so it is not an edge and the includes after it are still listed
reference.languageOfPlainH: C++ when the repository has any C++ source file, else C

dev: spdlog (benchmarks/repos), a small C project written for the fixtures

reference.what: the script found by the framework's own parser (@vue/compiler-sfc, svelte/compiler, @astrojs/compiler), its specifiers listed by ts.preProcessFile and resolved by ts.resolveModuleName with the repository's own tsconfig and the bundler resolution rules; a host shim lets TypeScript resolve ./X.vue as a module

PHP's own tokenizer for the top-level use statements, and Composer's own autoloader (composer dump-autoload --classmap-authoritative in a scratch copy, then ClassLoader::findFile) for the file that defines each class; dependencies are not installed. A require/include of a literal path is not read by the reference, so the graph's edges of that kind count as ones the reference lacks and precision is a lower bound
swiftc -emit-imported-modules for the modules a file imports, and swift package describe for the targets and the files each owns; an edge is a file importing a local target other than its own

csharp.title: C#
csharp.unmeasured: no compiler-grade reference was run: Roslyn or scip-dotnet needs the .NET SDK and a restore and build of the repository, which is not installed here

dart.title: Dart
dart.unmeasured: no compiler-grade reference was run: scip_dart needs the Dart SDK and, for riverpod, a Flutter SDK to resolve the workspace

lua.title: Lua
lua.unmeasured: no reference exists to run: Lua resolves a module by searching package.path, and the roots a project sets are not declared in the repository, so the resolver's roots are the only roots there are

gdscript.title: GDScript
gdscript.unmeasured: no reference exists to run: the engine is the only resolver and it is not installed

predictions.claim: C/C++ recall is at least 90%: the resolver searches the way the compiler does, and the compiler's include dirs are the ones registered
C/C++ precision is at least 80%: a platform branch the three configurations do not enable is an include the graph counts and the reference does not
component precision is at least 95%: a specifier either resolves to a file TypeScript also resolves it to, or not at all
component recall is at least 90%; the misses are the bundler aliases and .js-to-.ts mappings the JS resolver does not read
Swift module-level precision is at least 99%
Swift module-level recall is at least 99%
